definition: A structured review of one workload - the components that together deliver one business capability - against the five Well-Architected pillars, with the people who build and run it. Microsoft's online assessment and Azure Advisor are inputs; the output is a short, owned list of risks and recorded decisions. Repeat it quarterly and after major changes.
example: The checkout review took a morning and produced ten owned risks, four ADRs and a documented accepted single point of failure.

definition: A short document kept in the repository that records one architectural decision: its context, the decision, the consequences, and what would make you revisit it. It preserves the reasoning behind trade-offs so they are not re-argued every few months.
example: ADR-014 records why Service Bus stays on Standard and names the date and triggers for revisiting it.

definition: Listing, for each component of a workload, how it can fail, what users experience, how the failure is detected and what limits the damage - including failures you deliberately accept. The most valuable part of a Well-Architected Review.
example: The payment provider row: down or slow, users cannot pay, SLO burn alert, circuit breaker and a friendly retry message.
